title: Weighted duty rotation and concise handoff summaries for on-call
author: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: Rotation schedules at several customers skew when simple round-robin assignment ignores part-time schedules, skillset requirements, and nested on-call pools. The result is frequent reassigns, overloaded responders, and noisy handoffs. This PR introduces a weighted duty rotation model plus a compact, automated handoff summary generator that pulls recent incident context and recommended actions into a single, shareable blob. The change set is intentionally scoped to the slo-toolkit CLI and the on-call export utilities so customers can opt-in with a feature flag before UI work in the console. Highlights: 1) duty rotation weights: new configuration allows teams to assign numeric weights to people and pools (e.g., 1.0 for full-time, 0.5 for part-time, 1.5 for secondary-duty volunteers). The rotation algorithm normalizes weights and produces balanced schedules across a sliding window. 2) fairness window and PTO-awareness: scheduler consults the calendar-export endpoint (ICal/CalDAV token) and linear-style user availability annotations to avoid assigning people who have PTO blocks or are flagged unavailable for the period. 3) skill constraints and soft-preferences: rotations may include tags (database, infra, runtime) to preferentially schedule qualified responders; soft-preferences bias but do not block scheduling. 4) concise automated handoff summaries: when a shift change is imminent the toolkit generates a one-paragraph handoff that includes active alerts, top-5 recent errors, recent autoremediations, last 24h escalation history, and links to the canonical playbook snippets. Summaries are sanitized, redact PII by default, and can be exported as plain text, JSON, or an HTML snippet for calendar descriptions. 5) preview/what-if CLI: new `sloctl rotation preview` command shows the upcoming X rotations with weighted scoring and indicates why a person was chosen, plus a `--simulate-pto` flag. 6) incremental rollout & feature flag: feature gated behind `oncall-weighted-rotation` with telemetry for acceptance metrics (assignment churn, missed-ack rate, handoff-open-rate). Implementation notes: the scheduler is implemented as a deterministic pass that takes a seed and produces a canonical ordering; this enables reproducible previews and easier debugging. Handoff generator reuses existing telemetry collectors and the runbook-catalog indexing code in slo-toolkit, but adds a compact summarizer and sanitization pipeline. Testing and validation: unit tests cover weight normalization, calendar exclusion logic, and tag constraints. Integration tests run an end-to-end preview against a seeded synthetic calendar and alert set. A small-scale, canary rollout was run internally for 2 weeks with observed 18% reduction in assignment collisions and a 12% improvement in handoff-open-rate metric. Rollout plan: merged behind a feature flag; console integration tracked in a follow-up PR that will add a calendar export button and a trimmed HTML handoff card. Backwards compatibility: existing rotation specs still valid; teams that do not opt-in see no change. Related: ENG-8124 (scheduling fairness), PM-221 (on-call UX improvements).
